fields.why: Table 2 gives prevalences across 3 or more groups of sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race/ethnicity, education and income.
These are the SPDs with 3 or more compared groups. Sex is a pair, and marital status and household size are not SPDs.

CI overlap of 'any two estimates' is the only stated significance criterion, so the 'highest/lowest among' claims for age, race, education and income rest on it. The brief's blanket-method rule then gives per-group vs referent only, as A gave the SOGI entries, not side by side; A's notes concede the dependence.

brief_issues: As in mm7309a3: section F could say outright that 'highest/lowest' claims under a stated CI-overlap rule are per-group vs referent only, not side by side.
